feedback: Based only on iteration 0 evidence and design reasoning; this candidate has not raced and I state no outcome for it. In iteration 0 all 60 trials ended off-track with no completions. Mean RMS error was low (0.02 to 0.027 m), but max_error sat at the 0.06 m limit on every track. This means the robot is staying close to the line on average and makes sharp excursions on bends, which points to a response problem, not a steady offset. Progress of 0.09 to 0.18 means it leaves well before half the course. Widening the row to a 0.024 m half-span keeps the tape in view further off-centre, so it is the right test. Hold the widened row if progress rises on all three tracks compared with iteration 0. If max_error still reaches 0.06 on the oval with few line-loss events, the limit is yaw response rather than sensing, so move to lower yaw inertia (wheel_track 0.10 m or mass 0.6 kg). If line_loss_events cluster on the slalom, the sensor row is still too narrow for its sharper alternations, so try sensor_size 0.016 for more signal per sensor.
requested_changes: Keep the widened row (x = -0.024 to +0.024 m at y = 0.04 m) if progress improves on all three tracks versus iteration 0; this is the first geometry change requested in iteration 0.
If max_error still hits 0.06 m with low steering_oscillation after the row change, reduce yaw inertia by trying wheel_track 0.10 m (the reduction is from 0.12 m).
If line_loss_events concentrate on the slalom with the widened row, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same positions to increase the tape signal per sensor.
